title: automation: a flow with a top-level cycle passes os validate and build; detectCycles runs only at registration and has no author-time home
body:
domain:server#5 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5oc56xChD6Wrc4cGSt

Filing gate: ① out-of-scope finding of the #28893 dev (os-dev-report 6570600658), filed by `domain:server` seat 5. Graded by this seat: p3, the same class as #28893 (a flow the engine refuses at registration passes the author-time gate, and is silently not registered at boot). Graded under 「定级你可以自己决定」 (Leehom, 2026-11-01).

Reach: an author shipping a flow whose top-level graph has a cycle without a back edge (`start → a → b → a`).
Reader who acts: a `domain:server` seat, with the `domain:spec` seat if the check moves into spec.

## What happens

Measured by the #28893 dev: such a flow passes `os validate` / `os build` with exit 0. The engine refuses it at `registerFlow` via `detectCycles` (`packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-checks.ts` ~line 738), which is not exported from the package index. Spec has no exported DAG check beside `validateControlFlow` (region bodies are cycle-checked by `analyzeRegion`; the top level is not).

## Wanted

- Choose a home:
  - (a) a spec export beside `validateControlFlow` that `detectCycles` then calls (a spec card; ⛔ no copy); or
  - (b) a service-automation index export (a widening of that package's surface).
- Then add the author-time call in the same CLI gate PR #29043 adds (`flow-region-shape.ts`), with the engine's message.
- Tests red first; the back-edge case still passes.

Blocked-by: #28893 (PR #29043 adds the gate this extends).

Dedupe: searched `flow top-level cycle validate detectCycles`; none. **New.**

Links back: #28893, PR #29043.
